newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr static in Tokyo, impact from MOF limited.
newsitem.headline: Dlr static in Tokyo, impact from MOF limited.

text.p: 0610 GMT 2400 GMT NYK CLOSE

The dollar stood still at around 126 yen in late Tokyo on Wednesday, with remarks from Japanese Finance Ministry officials having a fleeting impact in pushing the dollar down due to bids below 126 yen, dealers said.
The market awaited remarks by senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara later in the day, but any impact would be limited as position takers generally kept their positions flat, they said.
"Persistent fears of BOJ intervention near 127 yen and investor demand for bargain-hunting below 126 yen are making trading motionless," said a Japanese bank dealer.
The dollar briefly slipped in early afternoon on remarks by Sakakibara, who expressed concerns about excessive falls in the yen that were out of line with fundamentals.
He also said recent movements were driven by dealers' expectations, which may turn out to be incorrect.
"Present exchange rates clearly deviate from economic fundamentals," Sakakibara, head of MOF's International Finance Bureau, told the Lower House of parliament's Finance Committee.

Sakakibara also said the recent weakening of the yen was not due to higher U.S. interest rates and lower Japanese rates. He is scheduled to speak at an annual meeting of the Forex Club in Tokyo at around 0940 GMT.
But many dealers were sceptical about how far his further remarks might succeed in pushing the dollar down.

"Position takers at Japanese banks, as a whole, have not taken any large positions in either way," said a senior trader at another Japanese bank. "Their strategy right now is to buy dollars at 125.50 yen and sell them above 126.50 yen," he said.
The dollar stayed in the middle of the range, he added.

The first Japanese bank dealer said dollar-bearish remarks from Sakakibara may momentarily nudge the dollar down below 126 yen. But relatively brisk buying demand from Japanese investors and securities houses could stop the dollar from falling much.
"There are some Japanese investors who are happy to buy dollars at around 125.50 yen," said one bank dealer.
There was also a rumour that a Japanese major public fund and an Asian bank had placed bids at around 126 yen.
Dealers said the dollar may continue to lack a clear sense of direction ahead the release of trade data both from Japan and the United Stated due out on Thursday.
A dealer in Singapore said offers from foreign funds were capping the dollar at around 126.30 yen earlier in the morning.

The greenback also failed to advance in Asia on profit-taking, after brief gains overnight on comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, who said the launch of the single European currency could cause a shift from mark-denominated investments to dollar-denominated investments.

Dealers said the weak mark trend could continue as long as there was an expectation that the single currency would start on time.---Singapore newsroom +65- 870-3083)---Tatsuo Ito in Tokyo 81-3-3432-1396
